title: EPA's 2025 ANNUAL REPORT | Environment Protection Agency (EPA-SL)
description:
Our 2025 Annual Report highlights the ongoing transformation of the Environment Protection Agency (EPA-SL) and the tangible results achieved since the launch of our Transformation Strategy (#EPATS) in January 2024. 

Last year, we accomplished significant milestones, including the completion of NDC 3.0, NBSAP 3.0, and the 7th National Biodiversity Report. 
We also initiated Sierra Leone's first Biennial Transparency Report and Technology Needs Assessment, established nine Chiefdom Environment Enforcement Committees, and launched the country's first National Pollutant Inventory, with the first draft now completed.

In the areas of compliance, enforcement, and environmental protection, we've made notable progress. In the past year, the #EPA conducted 1,184 monitoring inspections, dismantled 202 illegal river dredges, pursued 25 civil enforcement actions, and granted 83 new Environmental Impact Assessment licenses. 
We've successfully raised US$15 million in mine rehabilitation guarantees, bringing the total to US$26.2 million for 2026. Additionally, our internally generated revenue reached Le168 million, reflecting a Le14 million increase from the previous year.

Organisationally, we've made significant strides as well. The oneEPA database expanded from three interfaces to six, incorporating new Human Resource Management, Payroll, and Laboratory Database Management Systems at no extra cost to the Agency. We launched our third RAC Centre of Excellence in just two years, are nearing completion of the Southern Regional Office, and added eight new Land Cruisers to our fleet. 
We secured 30% financing to advance the EPA Headquarters project, signed 13 strategic partnership agreements, obtained about US$5 million in new grants, and received US$2.2 million along with Le10.4 million in direct donor support for 21 projects.
These achievements are a testament to the collective effort of everyone involved in the EPA’s transformation journey. 

We extend our gratitude to our dedicated staff, Board Members, the Minister Jiwoh Abdulai and Deputy Minister of Environment and Climate Change, the Chairman and members of the Environment Committee in Parliament, the Sierra Leone Police, the RSLAF, the Judiciary, and our international and local partners, local authorities, and communities. 
A special thanks goes to H.E the President, the Vice President, and the Chief Minister for their invaluable guidance and support. 
There's plenty more to explore in the report and even greater goals ahead.
